goal: As a SafeGuard technical sales rep, counter GasTech's ~$198K all-Honeywell quote for NovaPetro RFQ-2025-0472 with a vendor-diversified Rosemount 625IR + Dräger configuration. Deliver a compliance matrix CSV (Rosemount, Dräger and Honeywell competitor columns with datasheet evidence), a 10-15 slide counter-proposal deck, a pricing workbook (BOM, 5-year TCO, competitive comparison) and a 1-2 page internal strategy memo; the Emerson 625IR datasheet and KLM gas-detection standard had to be found online.
delivered: All four files in output/: Compliance_Matrix_RFQ-2025-0472.csv with PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL per requirement for Rosemount, Dräger and Searchpoint Optima Plus; a 12-slide deck recommending Rosemount 625IR + Polytron 8100 EC + REGARD 7000; a pricing workbook (Read Me, BOM, 5-Year TCO, Competitive Comparison); and an internal memo with pricing guardrails. Subagents retrieved the official Emerson datasheet (Rev AG) and the 6-page KLM PDF.
what_went_wrong: The agent never treated GasTech's 5-day/$8,500 commissioning for 36 detectors across two sites as under-scoped: it priced its own commissioning at 5 days too, so the deck, comparison sheet and memo all missed the under-scoping, change-order and aggressive 6-week delivery arguments (R3, R6, R7, R5), even though the staged quote says 'Seemed low to Bobby' and the pricing sheet gives $1,800/day. The subagent's datasheet extract (step 21) included the 15-year IR source warranty and the E1/E5/E6/KS certification codes, but the deliverables omitted both. The TCO never stated that Searchpoint needs field calibration, the warranty saving was computed on 36 rather than 24 units, HART 7 was not checked, and the memo gave Polytron a 6-week lead time instead of 4.

failed_items.why: TCO quantifies Rosemount's no-field-calibration advantage but contrasts it against a generic 'GasTech all-Honeywell quote' with assumed labor hours; it never states that Searchpoint Optima Plus requires periodic field calibration (judge).

Deck adopts SafeGuard's own 'Five-day commissioning + SAT dossier' (slide 12) and never flags GasTech's 5 days for 36 detectors across two sites (one greenfield) as under-scoped, despite the competitor CSV note 'Seemed low to Bobby'.

Vendor-diversified recommendation is present, but the rationale omits the 15-year IR source warranty (which the Emerson subagent reported at step 21) and never argues that multiple vendors give NovaPetro pricing and support leverage.

Timeline cites only the 8-week controller path, ignores the 4-week Rosemount/Polytron lead times from Internal_Product_Pricing (the memo wrongly says Polytron 6 weeks), gives no early-April PO or receipt date, and accepts GasTech's 6-week delivery claim without question (matrix GEN-08 marks it PASS).

Comparison sheet only says 'GasTech 5-day amount appears low; SafeGuard prices 5 engineer-days'; it does not contrast the $8,500 with the pricing sheet's $1,800/day x 8-10 days, does not flag the 6-week delivery as aggressive, and does not attribute the 'seemed low' note to Bobby Kim.

Memo mentions the unexplained gap between the $209,330 line items and the ~$198K total and dismisses the 18% discount as unsupported, but never assesses thin margins, under-scoped commissioning, change-order risk (Building C conduit) or aggressive delivery.

The subagent's datasheet extract (step 21) listed the E1/E5/E6/KS codes and the QT SIL2 option, but matrix row IR-05 cites the quick-start guide MS-00825 and leaves those codes out, and IR-06 does not quote the datasheet's SIL2 statement.

RFQ prefers HART 7; matrix row IR-08 marks Rosemount PASS on generic 'HART' without noting whether HART 7 is supported, although the agent flagged the missing HART revision for the Honeywell competitor.

Deliverables cite only the 5-year limited warranty, omitting the 15-year IR source warranty that the subagent reported, and they compute warranty savings on 36 units / SafeGuard's optional $28,800 rather than 24 IR units x $700 = $16,800.

subagent_notes: Two research subagents (Emerson 625IR datasheet; KLM standard) launched early. Both retrieved the right documents: the Emerson subagent returned full specs including the 15-year IR source warranty, the E1/E5/E6/KS codes, factory-calibration-for-life and the 5-year proof test; the KLM subagent noted that the official PDF is cut off at 6 of 13 pages. They helped retrieval, but the root agent dropped several of the returned facts when building the deliverables.
